serverui.title: Server
serverui.intro: The WireGuard interface and the firewall rules Kut manages. Read-only; change settings on the Settings tab.
serverui.apply_text: The configuration and firewall rules are written again from scratch. Connected devices stay connected.

fw.title: Firewall
fw.note: Kut manages only the KUT-* chains; it does not touch ufw or your other rules. While the chains are empty nothing passes (fail-closed).
fw.rules_intro: Every rule Kut writes carries a comment tag (kut:…); the counters are matched to rules by that tag and refresh every 5 seconds. Tap a row to see the exact iptables line.
fw.rules_empty: No rules yet: they appear here once you add an active device.
fw.simulated: dry-run: the counters are simulated, not read from iptables.
fw.chain_empty: No rules in this chain for this filter.
fw.copy_failed: Could not copy; select the text manually.

chain.forward: Traffic passing through the server. Kut's fixed rules sit at the top: replies are let through, device-to-device traffic goes to KUT-PEERS, internet traffic to KUT-INET, everything else from or to the VPN is dropped.
chain.input: Traffic addressed to the server itself; everything from the VPN interface goes to KUT-IN.
chain.postrouting: Address translation on the way out; VPN traffic goes to KUT-NAT.
chain.kut_peers: Device-to-device permissions from access profiles. Anything not accepted here is dropped.
chain.kut_in: Which server ports each device may reach (replies, ping, the panel for devices without a profile, profile rules).
chain.kut_icmp: ICMP errors (for example path MTU) are accepted only from a side of the flow they belong to.
chain.kut_inet: Internet access for devices that have it, with optional blocking of private networks.
chain.kut_nat: Devices with internet access leave with the server's address (MASQUERADE).

skel.fwd-out-drop: New traffic into the VPN: drop

serverui.conf_note: Private and preshared keys are masked.
